- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underreact to true price spikes; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for early spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward slope at 0.5–1% per day post-spike.
- If official event net supply is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model underestimates upside potential; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast mean for 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model overestimates downside; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if forecast is trending upward >1.5% per day for 3+ days, reduce slope by 0.2–0.5% per day to avoid overshoot.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early volatility (e.g., first 5 days deviate >±3%), adjust forecast to match sentiment volatility pattern — e.g., if sentiment is bullish, start with higher base.
- When policy_count > 0, model tends to underreact to policy-driven price shifts; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast if policy is bullish, subtract if bearish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture momentum; apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility by 0.3–0.7% per day.
